title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: CISA finally puts a number on the water campaign — more than 100 internet-exposed systems targeted in July
items.content_text: CISA published internet exposure reduction guidance on 26 August and, in doing so, quantified the campaign that has been running against the water sector since late July: more than 100 internet-exposed systems in the Water and Wastewater Systems Sector were targeted, most commonly programmable logic controllers wired directly to a cellular modem. That is the whole finding in one sentence — the affected utilities were not breached through a sophisticated chain, they were reachable. The guidance itself is short and blunt: take PLCs, HMIs and RTUs off the public internet, route every remote-access need through a managed gateway or VPN rather than connecting to the device, require unique credentials with phishing-resistant MFA, and re-scan your own external footprint on a schedule instead of assuming it has not changed.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: CISA Internet Exposure Reduction guidance — reported by TechCrunch, SecurityWeek and Bank Info Security
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Guidance published and reported 26 Aug 2026; the targeting activity it quantifies occurred during July 2026; verified 27 Aug 2026

items.title: What the attacks actually did: lost view, altered ladder logic, disabled alarms and pressure loss
items.content_text: The FBI alert underlying this campaign is specific about impact in a way that most public reporting is not. Actors reached internet-facing Rockwell Automation MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers, then modified or deleted project-file logic, manipulated what HMI and SCADA screens displayed, and disabled shutdown and alarm logic — creating unsafe conditions while operators saw normal readings. Reported consequences at affected utilities include loss of view, pressure loss and flooding. Utilities in at least a dozen states have reported possible intrusions since 27 July, and a coordinated action against more than 30 Minnesota community systems on 26–27 July forced one treatment plant offline and several crews onto manual control. There has been no widespread interruption of drinking-water or wastewater service.

items.title: FBI seizes the Chinese scanning and relay platforms that made attacker traffic look like it came from next door
items.content_text: The Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorised seizures on 26 August of two linked platforms, QScan and QTRouter, operated by a PRC state-sponsored group the government calls QTFY. QScan handled reconnaissance; QTRouter relayed intrusions through compromised routers and IoT devices so the traffic arrived from ordinary domestic addresses. Both platforms are now inoperable because the seized domains were hard-coded into the malware. Named victims are federal, and the attributed activity is separate from the campaign currently affecting water utilities. The relevance to a small utility is the relay layer: if you have ever reasoned that traffic from a US residential address is probably a customer, or allow-listed by geography, that logic never worked. It also means your own unpatched perimeter router is recruitable.
tags: Incident — Law-enforcement action against state-sponsored infrastructure

items.title: Washington sanctions an Iranian cyber network inside US critical infrastructure — but not the crew touching the controllers
items.content_text: Treasury designated an Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security-directed hacking network on 24 August, describing intrusion and data theft at US energy companies, defence contractors, healthcare providers, IT firms and banks since late 2023, with a related State Department reward notice. It is worth being precise about what this does and does not cover. The designated activity is espionage. The campaign that has been altering ladder logic and disabling alarms at water utilities since late July remains formally unattributed by CISA, even though press sourcing and several state officials have pointed to Iran-nexus actors. Two clusters, one suspected sponsor, only one of them named in an official document. Treat the attribution as unconfirmed and the targeting interest as very real.

items.title: CISA ran the same attack against a water utility and a government body — one caught it, the other never noticed
items.content_text: CISA advisory AA26-237A publishes red-team assessment results from a water and wastewater entity and a government organisation, run with comparable tradecraft. One detected and responded. The other did not notice a domain compromise. The advisory is unusually direct about the reason: the difference was not product spend — both had capable tooling — but whether anyone reviewed the output, whether identity events were correlated, and whether the response had been practised. For a water utility with a two-person IT team and a managed service provider, the transferable finding is uncomfortable but useful: the telemetry existed in both cases. Detection is a staffing and process question long before it is a budget question.
tags: Threat intel — Federal red-team assessment at a water utility

items.title: Five agencies warn AI-written scripts are reading Siemens S7 controllers, with water named a target sector
items.content_text: Joint advisory AA26-231A from NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA describes actors using AI assistance to build custom tooling from a well-documented open-source S7 library, querying internet-exposed Siemens S7 controllers in traffic that resembles legitimate monitoring. EPA’s presence on the byline is the signal: water is explicitly among the named sectors. The agencies assess the activity as reconnaissance and pre-positioning. The consequence for a small utility is that the informal protection of obscurity is gone — writing a working S7 query used to require someone who knew the protocol, and now it does not. Any S7 controller you have on a public address is being read by more people than last year.
tags: Threat intel — Joint federal advisory naming water as a target sector

items.title: 4,407 controllers are answering from the public internet — and 22 of them sit in the towns being attacked
items.content_text: Forescout’s Vedere Labs scanned for internet-reachable industrial controllers and found 4,407 responding, including a subset located in the same municipalities where water-utility intrusions were reported during July. The pairing is what makes the research worth reading rather than the headline count. Exposure at a small utility is almost never a decision anyone made: it is a cellular modem shipped with inbound management on, an integrator’s port-forward left in place after commissioning, or a remote site added without going through whatever process exists. The number to care about is not 4,407. It is how many of your own sites you can account for without running a scan to find out.

items.title: 1,140 industrial ransomware victims in a quarter, and none of them needed the control system touched
items.content_text: Dragos counted 1,140 ransomware incidents at industrial organisations in the second quarter of 2026, up around 12 percent on the first, and drew out a point that applies directly to water utilities: attackers do not need SCADA access to disrupt operations. Encrypting the systems that handle billing, customer service, laboratory information, work orders and regulatory reporting is enough to force a utility into manual working for days. Those systems rarely get the segmentation attention that the treatment plant does, and in smaller utilities they often share a domain, a backup target and an administrator account with everything else.

items.title: The NetScaler flaw is now confirmed exploited and in KEV — federal deadline 29 August
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-8452 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 26 August, moving the Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway issue from a patching recommendation to confirmed exploitation in the wild. The flaw is a heap overflow in SAML single sign-on parsing, rated CVSS 8.8, needing no login, and reachable when the appliance runs as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. Canada’s Cyber Centre saw indications of exploitation from around 17 August after a public proof of concept appeared. Larger water authorities and the managed service providers that support smaller utilities both run NetScaler in front of remote access — which frequently means the path an operator or integrator uses to reach SCADA.

items.title: Rockwell’s MicroLogix guidance includes a recovery step that erases the program — read it before you need it
items.content_text: Rockwell Automation has published guidance for MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 owners following the campaign against internet-facing controllers, covering how to detect tampering with project-file logic and how to restore a controller to a known state. The step that catches operators out is that the recommended recovery path can clear the program from the controller, which is only survivable if you hold a verified offline copy of the logic. Many small utilities do not: the only copy lives on an engineering laptop belonging to the integrator who commissioned the site. Establish that before an incident forces the question at two in the morning.

items.title: A Git server exploit in KEV — and for some utilities that server holds the only copy of the PLC logic
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-60004 to the KEV catalogue on 25 August after reports of exploitation in the wild. The flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, allows anyone with ordinary repository write access to plant an executable Git hook and run shell commands as the Gitea service account. Gitea 1.27.1 fixed it on 27 July. Self-hosted Gitea shows up in water utilities more often than people expect, usually stood up by an integrator or a single engineer to hold PLC projects, HMI screens and SCADA configuration. If that describes your environment, a low-privilege contractor account is a route to code execution on the machine holding your control logic. Federal remediation was due 28 August.

items.title: No login required and no patch coming — the Ebyte gateway advisory is a replacement decision
items.content_text: CISA advisory ICSA-26-237-06 covers the Ebyte NE2-D11 serial-to-Ethernet gateway, whose web management interface does not consistently enforce authentication before granting administrative functions. An unauthenticated remote attacker can read configuration, change settings, hijack sessions or disrupt operation. CISA notes the vendor acknowledged the reports, said a patch was in development, then stopped responding, so there is no fix status. Inexpensive serial gateways of this class are common in water systems: they are what someone reached for when an older flow meter, chlorine analyser or lift-station RTU needed to talk to a network, and they very rarely appear in a patch programme.

items.title: CVSS 10.0 on a Siemens edge gateway that is dual-homed by design
items.content_text: Siemens’ August advisory set includes a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to run code with elevated privileges. Ten Siemens advisories arrived in the same batch alongside Schneider Electric and Phoenix Contact publications. The reason a water utility should read past the score is placement: gateways like this exist specifically to move process data from the plant network out to a historian, a reporting platform or a vendor cloud service. That makes them dual-homed by definition, and often the single device with a route in both directions between the treatment network and everything else.

items.title: An exploited Windows IKE flaw — pre-authentication SYSTEM on the box terminating your site-to-site VPN
items.content_text: CISA added four exploited vulnerabilities to KEV on 18 August, including a Windows Internet Key Exchange flaw allowing pre-authentication code execution as SYSTEM. Microsoft shipped the fix in April, so the gap is deployment rather than availability. The placement is what matters for a utility: IKE runs on the hosts terminating site-to-site VPN tunnels, and those tunnels are frequently how a central SCADA system reaches remote lift stations, tanks and well sites, or how an integrator reaches the plant. Pre-authentication compromise of that endpoint puts an attacker exactly at the junction between the business network and the process network.

items.title: Draft legislation would give the EPA authority to assess water utilities and require fixes
items.content_text: A Senate bill introduced in August would give the Environmental Protection Agency mandatory assessment authority over water-system cybersecurity, with reported funding of around $300 million a year to support utilities in closing the gaps it finds. It is a direct response to the current campaign and to the long-standing observation that the water sector has guidance and voluntary programmes but no enforceable baseline. The bill has been introduced, not enacted, and its provisions may change substantially in committee — so treat it as a signal of direction rather than a compliance obligation. Separately, industry groups have been pressing Congress for a water-sector reliability organisation modelled on NERC.

items.title: The NSA is putting an ISA/IEC 62443 certificate in front of the controllers it buys
items.content_text: ISASecure announced a partnership with the National Security Agency to develop a High Criticality Component Security Assurance certification scheme, derived from its Component Security Assurance programme and grounded in ISA/IEC 62443-4-2. Once accepted, the NSA intends to use it when adding OT components to the National Security Systems product compliant list. Water utilities are not the buyer here, but they are downstream of the effect: when a large customer makes certification a purchase condition, vendors build to it and the requirement language migrates into everyone else’s specifications. That gives a utility drafting a SCADA or instrumentation tender a defensible standard to cite rather than inventing security requirements from scratch.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: ISA / ISASecure press release — corroborated by Automation World and ISSSource
